If you're still on the fence about installing macOS 27 Golden Gate, a massive batch of security patches from Apple might be enough to convince you. And if you plan to stay on an older version, you should install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.8 as soon as possible. Here's why.

Apple Patches Over 200 macOS Vulnerabilities

Apple today published the full security release notes for macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8, detailing more than 200 vulnerabilities fixed in these updates.

As with several recent macOS updates, Apple credited several AI-related security teams and researchers in the acknowledgments section, including OpenAI Codex Security, NVIDIA AI Red Team, and Anthropic Research.

The patches included in macOS 27 cover vulnerabilities that could allow a malicious app or attacker to execute arbitrary code with kernel or root privileges, escape the macOS sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper, modify protected system files, access sensitive user data, and more.

For example, an AVEVideoEncoder vulnerability could allow a sandboxed app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges; a UDF file system vulnerability could similarly allow an app to execute code at the kernel level. Apple also patched vulnerabilities that could lead to remote code execution via Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.

As for macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8, both updates patch many of the same vulnerabilities mentioned above, including multiple kernel-level, root privilege, sandbox escape, Gatekeeper bypass, and remote code execution flaws.

The older systems also include some additional patches not listed for macOS 27, including an ImageIO vulnerability in macOS Sequoia 15.8 that could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted image.

Here are links to the security content for each update:

  • About the security content of macOS Golden Gate 27
  • About the security content of macOS Tahoe 26.7
  • About the security content of macOS Sequoia 15.8

Will you upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate, or stick with macOS Tahoe 26? Let us know in the comments.
